final.title: Why reviewer training is not enough
final.body:
Reviewer training helps, but it is only one control. If the same approval rules are applied over and over, the failure is often not knowledge. It is repeatable logic, data entry, fatigue, or edge cases that a slide deck will not remove. Training can improve judgment; it does not change the workflow.

The useful question is simple: are most errors happening because the reviewer does not know the rule, or because the work still depends on the same manual checks every time? If it is the second case, you are looking at a workflow problem, not a classroom problem.

A plain example: if invoice or approval checks always follow the same sequence, a tired person can still miss one step. A repeatable rule check can catch that kind of miss. That is not a complaint about people. It is just how late afternoons work.

At Bareni, we focus on repeatable logic steps in small-business workflows, with human approval kept in place for exceptions and high-risk decisions. That is a policy choice, not a guarantee.

The next step is simple: identify one recurring decision step that follows the same logic each time, and note how often it appears. If it is truly repeatable, it belongs on the shortlist before you spend more time on training materials.
